chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abd al-Wahhab, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ismail al-Ju'fi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the one who touches a bone of a deceased person. He said: 'If it has been a year, there is no problem with it.'
ai.seo_question: Does touching a deceased person's bone make you impure if it has been buried for a year?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'istihlak' (transformation) or natural purification, where the passage of time renders the bone of a deceased person pure for touch. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling is significant for determining the status of remains during burial and funeral rites, distinguishing between fresh remains and those that have settled in the earth. It reflects the practical application of purity laws to organic matter, emphasizing that impurity is not permanent but subject to change over time.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abdul Wahhab, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Ismail Al Ju’fy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the one who touches a bone of a deceased. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When it was a year old, so there is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 13. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from ‘Abd al-Wahhab from Muhammad ibn abu Hamzah from Hisham ibn Salim from ’Isma‘il al-Ju’fiy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about touching the bones of a dead person. He (the Imam) said, ‘If it is after one year, it is not harmful.’”
